summary: Merger of AutoGen and Semantic Kernel into one framework, GA April 2026, adding multi-agent orchestration patterns (Magentic-One), an Agent Harness for long-horizon tasks, and MCP/A2A interoperability.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses CLI subprocesses (not API-based agents), so the orchestration patterns from this framework don't map directly. Harness concept is interesting but AgentForge's deterministic state machine already covers similar ground.

summary: LangGraph's checkpoint library v4.1.0 provides per-node checkpoint recovery; crashed workflows resume from the last successful super-step, with pending writes saved for completed sibling nodes.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — pattern is relevant to AgentForge's HID-186 (stage-level partial retry). The checkpoint-at-each-boundary approach could inform implementation. However HID-186 already tracks this capability theme; no new issue needed.

source: Self-improving coding agent reflection loops (2026 survey)
summary: Practitioner survey of generate-evaluate-revise loops for coding agents; notes that reflection without external grounding (e.g. test results) adds 2-3x token overhead without quality gain. Reflexion pattern stores verbal lessons from failures in episodic memory.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge's plan revision cycle (PlanReview → PlanRevision) and HID-186 partial retry already embody this pattern. HID-167 automatic retry also covers failure-driven re-execution. No additional gap identified.

source: Agent episodic/persistent memory landscape 2026 (Mem0, Letta, Zep)
summary: Survey of persistent memory approaches for agents in 2026: Mem0, Letta (persistent memory blocks in context), Zep. Anthropic 2026 context-engineering guidance treats memory as structured note-taking in external storage that survives session boundaries.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge has skill distillation for cross-run learning (shipped) and HID-188 tracks run-outcome episodic memory injection. This confirms the direction is correct; no new gap identified.

source: OpenAI Agents SDK April 2026 update (sandboxing, subagents)
summary: OpenAI Agents SDK April 2026 update added sandboxed code execution, subagent spawning, and improved handoffs. TypeScript subagent support still in roadmap. Assistants API retired Aug 2026, replaced by Agents API (public beta Sept 2026).
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses CLI subprocesses (claude, codex), not OpenAI's API-based SDK. The handoff pattern is interesting but doesn't map to AgentForge's deterministic state machine without a significant rewrite.

summary: Karpathy described 'agentic engineering' as his Feb 2026 successor to vibe coding: orchestrating agents (Claude, Codex) as the primary mode with humans acting as oversight. Agent stack primitives: agents, subagents, prompts, memory, permissions, tools, skills, hooks, MCP.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — conceptually validates AgentForge's design. The specific stack primitives (skills, hooks, MCP) echo what AgentForge already implements. No concrete implementation gap identified; more of an architectural affirmation.

source: GitHub trending agent repos August 2026 (DeepSeek Harness, multica)
summary: August 2026 GitHub trending: DeepSeek Harness (dsh) gained 191k stars — an agent harness described as developer preview. multica-ai/multica positions as open-source managed-agents platform for assigning tasks and tracking progress with coding agents.

source: General AI agent orchestration landscape survey 2026
summary: 2026 landscape: LangGraph, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, and Microsoft Agent Framework are the main orchestration options. Gartner predicts 40% of enterprise apps will embed task-specific AI agents by end of 2026. Most teams pick one of these four frameworks.
